topic.subject: science
topic.title: Motion and time
topic.scope: speed, uniform and non-uniform motion, measuring time, distance-time graphs, simple pendulum

misconceptions.statement: Time is an absolute concept that exists independently of any periodic event.
misconceptions.why: Students experience time as a continuous flow in daily life without needing to observe a clock.
misconceptions.fix: Time is measured by counting the repetitions of a periodic event, such as the swing of a pendulum or the rotation of the Earth.

probe.question: If all clocks and watches in the world stopped, would time still exist?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, time would keep passing exactly the same way.

misconceptions.statement: A pendulum takes longer to complete a swing if it is pulled further away.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the distance traveled (amplitude) with the time period of the oscillation.
misconceptions.fix: For small oscillations, the time period of a simple pendulum depends only on its length, not on the amplitude.

probe.question: If you pull a pendulum bob further to the side before releasing it, what happens to the time it takes to complete one oscillation?
probe.wrong_answer: It will take more time because it has to cover a longer distance.

misconceptions.statement: An object that moves faster always covers more distance in the same amount of time.
misconceptions.why: Students often fail to distinguish between the concept of speed as a rate and distance as a total quantity.
misconceptions.fix: Speed is defined as the distance covered per unit time; if an object is faster, it covers more distance in a specific time interval.

probe.question: If two cars travel for the same amount of time, how do we know which one is faster?
probe.wrong_answer: The one that traveled the longest distance is the fastest.

misconceptions.statement: Uniform motion means the object is moving in a straight line.
misconceptions.why: The word 'uniform' is often associated with straightness or lack of change in direction in everyday language.
misconceptions.fix: Uniform motion means an object moves along a straight line with a constant speed, meaning it covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.

probe.question: If a car moves in a circle at a constant speed of 40 km/h, is it in uniform motion?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because its speed is constant.

misconceptions.statement: The shape of a distance-time graph is a picture of the path the object took.
misconceptions.why: Students tend to interpret graphs as literal maps or sketches of the physical trajectory of the object.
misconceptions.fix: A distance-time graph represents the relationship between distance and time, not the physical path or shape of the road.

probe.question: If a car travels on a curved road, what will its distance-time graph look like?
probe.wrong_answer: The graph will be curved like the road.
